definition_zh: 机场；航空港
definition_en: a place where aircraft take off and land, with buildings for passengers and cargo
core_image: 跑道尽头一排灯火，航站楼的玻璃幕墙映着起落的机影
scene: 凌晨的出发大厅里，人们拖着箱子排队，广播一遍遍报着登机口。She arrived at the airport two hours before the flight.
sceneCN: 这里 airport 是「机场」（第 1 个义项：供飞机起降的场地与设施）；句意为她在航班起飞前两小时到了机场。图中可辨识物件：出发大厅、行李箱、航班信息牌。

pos.zh: 名词：机场；航空港

derivatives.zh: 由本词与 tax 合成的名词，义为「机场税」
由本词与 lounge 合成的名词，义为「机场休息室」

senses.title: The place where planes take off
senses.definition: a place with runways and buildings where aircraft take off and land
senses.definitionCN: 设有跑道与相关建筑、供飞机起飞降落的场所
senses.example: She arrived at the airport two hours before the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 她在航班起飞前两小时到了机场。
senses.why: The word joins air to port in the sense of a harbour, so an airport is literally a harbour for aircraft rather than ships.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 air 与 port「港口」结合在一起，所以 airport 字面上就是飞机的港口，而不是船的港口。

senses.title: The whole transport complex
senses.titleCN: 航空港（整套设施与枢纽）
senses.definition: the entire complex of terminals, cargo areas, customs, and services that makes up an air transport hub
senses.definitionCN: 由航站楼、货运区、海关与服务设施共同构成的空运枢纽
senses.example: The new airport handles both passengers and freight.
senses.exampleCN: 新航空港同时处理旅客与货运。
senses.why: As air travel grew, the simple landing field became a city-like complex, and the word widened to cover the whole hub.
senses.whyCN: 随着航空发展，简单的起降场变成了城市般的综合体，这个词也随之扩指整个枢纽。

intro.en: Airport is a twentieth-century compound that borrows the word for a harbour and moves it into the sky.
intro.cn: airport 是二十世纪的复合词，借用了「港口」这个词，把它搬到了天上。

items.en: Portus meant 'harbour, haven', the source of port and of the -port in airport and seaport.
items.cn: portus 意为「港口、避风处」，port 以及 airport、seaport 中的 -port 都源于它。

items.en: English port first meant a harbour and later a town with a harbour.
items.cn: 英语 port 最初指港口，后来指有港口的城镇。

items.en: With powered flight, airport was coined on the model of seaport for a place where aircraft land.
items.cn: 随着动力飞行出现，人们仿照 seaport 造出 airport，指飞机降落之地。

items.en: The word widened from a landing field to the terminal buildings and the whole transport complex.
items.cn: 这个词从起降场扩展指航站楼乃至整套交通设施。

items.en: Airport now contrasts with airfield: the first is commercial and built up, the second often small and plain.
items.cn: 如今 airport 与 airfield 形成对照：前者是商业化的成片设施，后者常是小而简易的场地。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other -port words; the near-meaning group gathers aviation places of different size.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 -port 结尾的词；近义组收规模不同的航空场所。

entries.definition: A port where ships load and unload, the model for airport.
entries.definitionCN: 供船只装卸的港口，正是 airport 的造词样板。

entries.definition: A place where helicopters land and take off.
An official document allowing a person to travel abroad.
entries.definitionCN: 允许个人出国旅行的官方证件。

entries.definition: An area of land with runways, often without large terminal buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 有跑道的场地，通常没有大型航站楼。

entries.definition: The building at an airport where passengers arrive and depart.
entries.definitionCN: 机场中旅客进出港的建筑。

entries.definition: A formal or older word for a small airfield.
entries.definitionCN: 指小型机场的正式或较旧说法。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: air and port, the Latin word for a harbour.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：air 与表示港口的拉丁词 port。

normal.en: Seaport is for ships, airport is for planes: the same harbour word moves into the sky.
normal.cn: seaport 给船用，airport 给飞机用：同一个「港口」词搬到了天上。

normal.en: A heliport follows the same pattern for helicopters.
normal.cn: heliport 用同样的方式为直升机造词。

normal.en: The stress is on air: AIR-port.
normal.cn: 重音在 air 上：AIR-port。

normal.en: An airfield is smaller and plainer than an airport.
normal.cn: airfield 比 airport 更小、更简陋。

normal.en: Keep both parts whole in spelling: no dropped p, no hyphen.
normal.cn: 拼写时两个部件都要完整：不能丢掉 p，也不加连字符。

abstract.en: Calling a runway a harbour shows how new technology is named with old geography.
abstract.cn: 把跑道叫作港口，说明新技术是如何用旧地理词汇命名的。

abstract.en: An airport is a place built for leaving, yet most of it is designed to make waiting bearable.
abstract.cn: 机场是为离开而建的地方，可它的大部分设计都是为了让等待可以忍受。

abstract.en: The shift from airfield to airport records the moment aviation became an industry.
abstract.cn: 从 airfield 到 airport 的变化，记录了航空变成产业的那一刻。

examples.en: She arrived at the airport two hours before the flight.
examples.cn: 她在航班起飞前两小时到了机场。

examples.en: The new airport handles both passengers and freight.
examples.cn: 新航空港同时处理旅客与货运。

examples.en: Fog closed the airport for most of the morning.
examples.cn: 大雾让机场关闭了大半个上午。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱儿泡特」——爱儿泡特一下飞机，就站在机场门口等车。

root: 由 air「空气」与 port「港口」复合而成，仿 seaport 造词，字面即「航空之港」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses describe the same place: one as ground for aircraft, one as a whole hub for people and freight.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项描述的是同一个地方：一个是飞机的起降场地，一个是人与货物的整体枢纽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of runway lights, with a glass terminal reflecting the planes that pass.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑道尽头一排灯火，玻璃航站楼映着来往的飞机。

branches.en: a plane touching down in the rain
branches.cn: 在雨中触地的飞机

branches.en: a shuttle bus circling the runway road
branches.cn: 绕跑道公路行驶的班车

branches.en: a cargo hall stacked with pallets
branches.cn: 堆满货板的货运大厅

branches.en: a customs queue at dawn
branches.cn: 清晨的海关队伍

branches.en: one harbour, first for planes and then for trade
branches.cn: 同一个港口，先为飞机而设，后为贸易而设

intro.en: The element air, the Latin harbour word port, and the compounds built on them.
intro.cn: 成分 air、拉丁语中表示港口的 port，以及建在其上的复合词。

latinIntro.en: portus is recorded Latin; the compound airport itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: portus 是有文献记录的拉丁词，而复合词 airport 本身是近代英语的产物。

items.meaning: a fee charged at an airport
a waiting room at an airport

definition_zh: 警报器；闹钟；警报；惊恐；使惊慌
definition_en: a device or signal that warns of danger, sudden fear, or to make someone frightened
core_image: 深夜走廊里一只红色蜂鸣器突然亮起，光在墙上抖
scene: 凌晨三点，走廊里的蜂鸣器突然响起来，所有人都被惊醒。The fire alarm woke everyone in the building.
sceneCN: 这里 alarm 是「警报器」（第 1 个义项：发出声响以警告危险的装置）；句意为火警警报器把楼里所有人都吵醒了。图中可辨识物件：蜂鸣器、走廊、应急灯。

pos.zh: 名词：警报器；闹钟；警报；惊恐
动词：使惊慌；使担忧

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人惊慌的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「惊人地；令人担忧地」
由本词加表人后缀构成，义为「危言耸听者」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「惊慌的；担忧的」

senses.title: A warning device
senses.definition: a device that makes a loud noise to warn people of danger or to wake them
senses.definitionCN: 发出巨响以警告危险或唤醒人的装置
senses.example: The fire alarm woke everyone in the building.
senses.exampleCN: 火警警报器把楼里所有人都吵醒了。
senses.why: The word began as a shout, and the device inherited the shout: what once called people to arms now calls them out of bed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本是一声喊叫，装置继承了那声喊叫：从前喊人拿起武器，如今喊人起床。

senses.title: A warning signal
senses.definition: a sound or message that warns people of approaching danger
senses.definitionCN: 提醒人们危险临近的声音或讯息
senses.example: The sirens sounded an air-raid alarm across the city.
senses.exampleCN: 警报声在全城拉响了空袭警报。
senses.why: This sense keeps the message rather than the machine: the alarm is the warning itself, whether or not a device produces it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留的是讯息而非机器：alarm 就是警告本身，不管是不是由装置发出。

senses.title: Sudden fear
senses.definition: sudden fear caused by the awareness of danger
senses.definitionCN: 意识到危险时突然产生的恐惧
senses.example: She looked up in alarm when the door slammed.
senses.exampleCN: 门砰地关上时，她惊慌地抬起头。
senses.why: Before there were sirens, alarm named the feeling a sudden cry produced in the chest, and that older sense survives in in alarm.
senses.whyCN: 在警报器出现之前，alarm 指的是突然的喊声在胸口引起的那种感觉，这个旧义仍保存在 in alarm 里。

senses.title: To make someone anxious
senses.definition: to make someone feel worried or frightened
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到担忧或害怕
senses.example: The drop in sales alarmed the board.
senses.exampleCN: 销量下滑让董事会感到不安。
senses.why: The verb reverses the direction: instead of feeling the cry, you become the thing that sets it off in others.
senses.whyCN: 动词把方向反过来：不再是听见喊声的人，而是让别人心里响起喊声的那一方。

intro.en: Alarm began as an Italian shout meaning 'to arms', and it still carries that urgency inside it.
intro.cn: alarm 最初是一句意大利语的呼喊，意为「拿起武器」，至今仍带着那股紧迫感。

items.en: The cry all'arme meant 'to arms!', what a watchman shouted when enemies approached.
items.cn: all'arme 意为「拿起武器！」，是守夜人发现敌人逼近时的呼喊。

items.en: French took the cry as alarme, naming both the shout and the fear it caused.
items.cn: 法语把这声呼喊借作 alarme，既指喊声，也指它引起的恐惧。

items.en: English borrowed it in the fourteenth century, first as a call to arms and then as any warning.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入，先指「召人御敌的号令」，后泛指任何警告。

items.en: The word spread to bells, drums and clocks, and the mechanical alarm clock appears in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到钟、鼓与时钟，机械闹钟在十七世纪出现。

items.en: The emotional sense survives mainly in in alarm and take alarm, while the device sense dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 情绪义主要保存在 in alarm 与 take alarm 中，装置义则在日常使用中占主导。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on alarm; the near-meaning group gathers warnings and sudden fears.
note.cn: 形近组收由 alarm 构成的词；近义组收警告与突发恐惧类词。

entries.definition: Causing worry or fear, often said of a trend.
entries.definitionCN: 引起担忧或恐惧的，常形容某种趋势。

entries.definition: A person who spreads exaggerated warnings of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 散布夸大危险警告的人。

entries.definition: Frightened or worried by something.
Words or a sign that tell people about possible danger.
entries.definitionCN: 告知可能危险的话语或标志。

entries.definition: A loud device that makes a long wailing sound as a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 发出长鸣作为警告的响亮装置。

entries.definition: Sudden uncontrolled fear that spreads through a group.
entries.definitionCN: 在人群中蔓延的突然失控的恐惧。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the Italian cry all'arme and its French reshaping.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：意大利语呼喊 all'arme 及其法语改写形式。

normal.en: Alarm was once a shout: all'arme means 'to arms', so the word still sounds urgent.
normal.cn: alarm 原本是一声喊：all'arme 意为「拿起武器」，所以这个词至今听起来紧急。

normal.en: The device and the feeling share one word because a cry produces both.
normal.cn: 装置与情绪共用一个词，因为一声呼喊同时产生两者。

normal.en: An alarm clock is a shout that comes from a small box.
normal.cn: 闹钟就是从一个小盒子里发出的那声大喊。

normal.en: In alarm keeps the old emotional sense; set the alarm uses the new device sense.
normal.cn: in alarm 保留古老的情绪义；set the alarm 用的是装置义。

normal.en: One l, then a: a-l-a-r-m, not allarm.
normal.cn: 一个 l 后接 a：a-l-a-r-m，不是 allarm。

abstract.en: A word born as a battle cry now wakes people for work, which is a small history of peace.
abstract.cn: 一个诞生于战场的词如今唤人上班，这本身就是一小段和平史。

abstract.en: Alarm is designed to interrupt: its whole purpose is to break whatever you were doing.
abstract.cn: 警报的设计目的就是打断：它存在的意义就是中止你正在做的事。

abstract.en: A false alarm is a reminder that the feeling and the fact can come apart.
abstract.cn: 虚惊一场提醒我们：感受与事实可以彼此脱节。

examples.en: The fire alarm woke everyone in the building.
examples.cn: 火警警报器把楼里所有人都吵醒了。

examples.en: She looked up in alarm when the door slammed.
examples.cn: 门砰地关上时，她惊慌地抬起头。

examples.en: The drop in sales alarmed the board.
examples.cn: 销量下滑让董事会感到不安。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，拉姆」——额，拉姆一按按钮，整栋楼都响起了警报。

root: 源自意大利语呼喊 all'arme「拿起武器」，经法语 alarme 进入英语，由「召人御敌的号令」引申为警报器、警报与惊恐。

sensesIntro.en: One cry runs through all four senses: the device that makes it, the message it carries, the fear it plants, and the act of setting it off in others.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项贯穿着同一声呼喊：发出呼喊的装置、呼喊携带的讯息、呼喊种下的恐惧，以及让别人心里响起呼喊的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red buzzer lights up in a dark corridor and the light shakes on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：深夜走廊里一只红色蜂鸣器亮起，光在墙上抖动。

branches.en: a clock ringing at half past six
branches.cn: 六点半响起的闹钟

branches.en: a siren rising over the rooftops
branches.cn: 越过屋顶的警报声

branches.en: a face turned suddenly towards a noise
branches.cn: 被响声惊得猛然转过去的脸

branches.en: a chart that makes a board sit up
branches.cn: 让董事会坐直身子的那张图表

branches.en: one cry, heard as an object and felt as a state
branches.cn: 同一声呼喊，既被当作器物，也被感受为状态

intro.en: An Italian phrase, its French reshaping, and the English endings built on the borrowed noun.
intro.cn: 一个意大利短语、它的法语改写，以及建在这个借词上的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The phrase is Italian, not Latin, though arme goes back to Latin arma, 'weapons', so the Latin list has one entry.
latinIntro.cn: 这个短语属意大利语而非拉丁语，但 arme 可追到拉丁语 arma「武器」，因此拉丁词条只列一个。

definition_zh: 虽然；尽管
definition_en: although, used to introduce a phrase that admits something while qualifying the main statement
core_image: 一句话说完，又回头补上一句「虽然如此」，把话说得更稳
scene: 方案被改得只剩三页，讨论却还没开始。The plan was accepted, albeit with several conditions.
sceneCN: 这里 albeit 是「虽然、尽管」（第 1 个义项：引导让步短语，表示前面的话要打个折扣）；句意为方案被接受了，尽管附有几个条件。图中可辨识物件：三页方案、长桌、批注笔。

pos.zh: 连词：虽然；尽管

derivatives.zh: albeit 的原始三词形式，义为「尽管它是……」
同一构词模式的古旧连词，义为「虽然；然而」

senses.title: Although, before a phrase
senses.definition: although, used chiefly before an adjective, adverb, or prepositional phrase to concede a point
senses.definitionCN: 意为「虽然」，多用于形容词、副词或介词短语之前，表示让步
senses.example: The plan was accepted, albeit with several conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 方案被接受了，尽管附有几个条件。
senses.why: Albeit is a compressed clause, 'all be it', so it can carry only a small phrase: what follows is the thing that 'is' conceded.
senses.whyCN: albeit 是一个压缩的从句「all be it」，所以只能带一个小短语：后面跟的就是被承认「是」的那一点。

senses.title: Although, before a full clause, in older use
senses.titleCN: 虽然（后接完整从句的古旧用法）
senses.definition: in older writing, although, used before a full clause with its own subject and verb
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧的文字中意为「虽然」，后面可以接带主语和动词的完整从句
senses.example: Albeit he was tired, he stayed until the end.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管他很累，还是留到了最后。
senses.why: Because the word still contains 'it', older writers could let a whole clause follow; modern usage prefers although for that job.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词里仍含有 it，旧时作者可以接一整个从句；现代用法则把这个任务交给 although。

intro.en: Albeit is a whole clause worn down into one word: 'all be it' became a single concessive conjunction.
intro.cn: albeit 是一整个从句磨损成一个词：「all be it」变成了单一的让步连词。

items.en: The phrase all be it meant 'though it be all (that)', a concessive clause used after a statement.
items.cn: 短语 all be it 意为「尽管它是这样」，是放在陈述之后的让步从句。

items.en: Reduced forms such as al be it appear in the fourteenth century, with al as a variant of all.
items.cn: 十四世纪出现 al be it 这类缩减形式，其中 al 是 all 的变体。

items.en: The three words fuse into albeit, and the new word is felt as a single conjunction.
items.cn: 三个词融合成 albeit，新词被当作一个整体连词来使用。

items.en: Albeit is common in formal prose, often introducing a short phrase rather than a clause.
items.cn: albeit 在正式散文中常见，多引导短短语而不是完整从句。

items.en: The word survives mainly in careful writing, where its brevity is valued over the plainer although.
items.cn: 这个词主要活在讲究的文字里，人们看重它比 although 更简洁。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same 'be it' pattern; the near-meaning group gathers concessive connectors.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「be it」模式构成的词；近义组收表示让步的连接词。

entries.definition: An archaic conjunction meaning although or nevertheless.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧连词，意为「虽然」或「然而」。

entries.definition: An archaic conjunction meaning provided that.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧连词，意为「只要；倘若」。

entries.definition: The standard conjunction for conceding a fact before the main clause.
entries.definitionCN: 在主句前承认某一事实的标准连词。

entries.definition: A shorter and more informal form of although, also usable at the end of a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: although 更短更口语的形式，也可放在句末。

entries.definition: Used to contrast two facts, more neutral than a concession.
entries.definitionCN: 用于对比两项事实，比让步更中性。

normalIntro.en: Three real words carry it: all, be, and it, worn down into one conjunction.
normalIntro.cn: 三个真实词承载它：all、be、it，磨损成一个连词。

normal.en: Albeit is all be it: say the three words fast and the conjunction appears.
normal.cn: albeit 就是 all be it：把三个词连快说，连词就出来了。

normal.en: Because it contains be, it likes short phrases rather than full clauses.
normal.cn: 因为里面含有 be，它更爱接短短语而不是完整从句。

normal.en: Albeit is one word, never two: no comma inside it.
normal.cn: albeit 是一个词，不是两个：中间不加逗号。

normal.en: Use albeit for a concession you want to keep brief; use although when a clause follows.
normal.cn: 想简短地让一步就用 albeit；后面跟完整从句时用 although。

normal.en: The stress falls at the end: al-BE-it.
normal.cn: 重音落在末尾：al-BE-it。

abstract.en: A three-word clause collapsed into one word shows how grammar compresses repeated thought.
abstract.cn: 三个词的从句缩成一个词，说明语法会压缩反复出现的想法。

abstract.en: Albeit admits a limitation without withdrawing the claim, which is a very precise social move.
abstract.cn: albeit 承认一个限制，却不撤回主张，这是一种非常精确的社交动作。

abstract.en: The word now sounds formal because plain although does the same work more cheaply.
abstract.cn: 这个词如今显得正式，因为朴素的 although 用更低的成本完成了同样的事。

examples.en: The plan was accepted, albeit with several conditions.
examples.cn: 方案被接受了，尽管附有几个条件。

examples.en: He agreed to help, albeit reluctantly.
examples.cn: 他同意帮忙，尽管很不情愿。

examples.en: The team won the match, albeit by a single point.
examples.cn: 球队赢了比赛，尽管只赢了一分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「噢，必特」——噢，必特先生答应了，虽然有点勉强。

root: 源自中古英语短语 all be it「尽管它是」，三个词融合为一个让步连词。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses concede a point; the only difference is how much grammar the word is allowed to carry after it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都在让一步，区别只在于这个词后面能带多少语法成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence finishes, then a hand goes back to add 'even so' at the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话说完，一只手又回去在边上补一句「即便如此」。

branches.en: a yes followed by a list of conditions
branches.cn: 一个「同意」后面跟着一串条件

branches.en: a slow yes, said with a sigh
branches.cn: 叹着气说出的那个「好」

branches.en: an old sentence with a full clause after it
branches.cn: 后面接着完整从句的旧式句子

branches.en: a page of seventeenth-century prose
branches.cn: 十七世纪散文的一页

branches.en: one concession, now short and now long
branches.cn: 同一个让步，有时短，有时长

intro.en: Three ordinary English words fused into a single conjunction.
intro.cn: 三个普通英语单词融合成一个连词。

latinIntro.en: Every part is native English; there is no Latin layer, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 每个成分都是英语本族词，没有拉丁语层，因此拉丁词条列表为空。

definition_zh: 酒精；乙醇；含酒精饮料；（化学）醇
definition_en: the colourless liquid in drinks that makes people drunk, drinks containing it, or a class of chemical compounds
core_image: 一只玻璃瓶里透明的液体，标签上只有一行成分说明
scene: 餐桌上摆着一排玻璃杯，有人正往里倒透明液体，冰块碰出轻响。The doctor asked how much alcohol he drank each week.
sceneCN: 这里 alcohol 是「酒精、含酒精饮料」（第 2 个义项：含有乙醇的饮品）；句意为医生问他每周喝多少酒。图中可辨识物件：玻璃杯、冰块、酒瓶。

pos.zh: 名词：酒精；乙醇；含酒精饮料；（化学）醇

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「含酒精的；酗酒的」
由本词加表示病态的 suffix 构成，义为「酒精中毒；酗酒成瘾」
由本词与 free 合成，义为「不含酒精的」

senses.title: The intoxicating substance itself
senses.definition: the colourless liquid, ethanol, that is the active substance in drinks and is also used as a solvent
senses.definitionCN: 无色液体乙醇，是酒类中的有效成分，也用作溶剂
senses.example: This cleaner contains alcohol and should not be used near a flame.
senses.exampleCN: 这种清洁剂含酒精，不应在明火附近使用。
senses.why: This is the chemical sense, and it comes straight from the Arabic word for a fine powder once used as eye make-up: the liquid was first obtained by distillation.
senses.whyCN: 这是化学义，直接来自阿拉伯语中一种曾作眼影的细粉之名：这种液体最早正是通过蒸馏取得的。

senses.title: Drinks that contain it
senses.definition: drinks such as beer, wine, or spirits that contain ethanol
senses.definitionCN: 啤酒、葡萄酒、烈酒等含乙醇的饮品
senses.example: The doctor asked how much alcohol he drank each week.
senses.exampleCN: 医生问他每周喝多少酒。
senses.why: Since the substance is what makes a drink alcoholic, the name of the substance became a general word for the drinks themselves.
senses.whyCN: 既然正是这种物质让饮品带酒劲，物质之名便成了一类饮品的总称。

senses.title: A class of chemical compounds
senses.definition: in chemistry, any of a large class of organic compounds containing a hydroxyl group
senses.definitionCN: 化学中含有羟基的一类有机化合物
senses.example: Sugar alcohols are used as sweeteners in many processed foods.
senses.exampleCN: 糖醇被用作许多加工食品的甜味剂。
senses.why: Chemists generalised the name from ethanol to the whole family, so any compound built on the same pattern counts as an alcohol.
senses.whyCN: 化学家把这个名字从乙醇推广到整个家族，凡是按同一结构组成的化合物都算一种 alcohol。

intro.en: Alcohol began as an Arabic word for a fine powder used as eye make-up, and only later became the name of a distilled liquid.
intro.cn: alcohol 原是一个阿拉伯语词，指用作眼影的细粉，后来才成为蒸馏液体的名称。

items.en: Al-kuhl named a fine powder of antimony used to darken the eyelids, and by extension anything finely refined.
items.cn: al-kuḥl 指一种用于描黑眼睑的锑粉，并引申指任何精细提炼之物。

items.en: Alchemists borrowed the word for a finely purified substance, and used it for spirits obtained by distillation.
items.cn: 炼金术士借这个词指精细提纯之物，并用它称呼蒸馏所得的烈性液体。

items.en: English alcohol first names a powder and then, from the sixteenth century, a distilled spirit.
items.cn: 英语 alcohol 先指粉末，十六世纪起指蒸馏酒。

items.en: Chemistry fixed the word on ethanol, the substance in wine and beer that causes drunkenness.
items.cn: 化学把这个词固定在乙醇上，即葡萄酒与啤酒中致醉的那种物质。

items.en: The word widened again to drinks in general and to the whole chemical class of alcohols.
items.cn: 这个词再度扩展，既泛指酒类，也指整个醇类化合物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on alcohol; the near-meaning group gathers the substance and the drinks in other words.
note.cn: 形近组收由 alcohol 构成的词；近义组收这种物质与酒类的其他说法。

entries.definition: Containing alcohol, or a person dependent on it.
entries.definitionCN: 含酒精的，或指对酒精依赖的人。

entries.definition: The illness of being unable to control one's drinking.
A related class of chemical compounds, named from alcohol and dehydrogenated.
entries.definitionCN: 一类相关化合物，名称由 alcohol 与「脱氢」缩合而成。

entries.definition: The precise chemical name for the alcohol in drinks.
entries.definitionCN: 酒类中所含酒精的精确化学名称。

entries.definition: Strong distilled drink such as whisky or gin.
entries.definitionCN: 威士忌、金酒之类的蒸馏烈酒。

entries.definition: Strong alcoholic drinks, in a formal or trade sense.
entries.definitionCN: 烈酒，多用于正式或行业语境。

normalIntro.en: Two real layers carry the word: Arabic al-kuhl, a fine powder, and the alchemists' use of it for distilled liquid.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实层次承载这个词：阿拉伯语 al-kuḥl 指细粉，以及炼金术士用它称呼蒸馏液。

normal.en: The al- at the start is the Arabic article, the same one as in algebra and alchemy.
normal.cn: 开头的 al- 是阿拉伯语冠词，与 algebra、alchemy 中的那个 al- 是同一个。

normal.en: The word travelled from eye make-up to distilled liquid to the drinks on the table.
normal.cn: 这个词从眼影走到蒸馏液，再走到餐桌上的酒。

normal.en: Chemists kept the name for the whole family, so methanol and sugar alcohols count too.
normal.cn: 化学家把名字留给了整个家族，所以甲醇与糖醇也算。

normal.en: Alcohol is uncountable for the substance and countable for the chemical compounds.
normal.cn: 指这种物质时不可数，指具体化合物时可数。

normal.en: Do not double the l: a-l-c-o-h-o-l.
normal.cn: 不要写双 l：a-l-c-o-h-o-l。

abstract.en: A word for cosmetics became a word for chemistry and then for a social problem, which is a long journey for one noun.
abstract.cn: 一个化妆品词变成化学词，又变成社会问题词，这对一个名词来说是很长的旅程。

abstract.en: The same substance is a solvent, a drink and a health risk, and the word refuses to separate them.
abstract.cn: 同一种物质既是溶剂、又是饮品、又是健康风险，而这个词拒绝把它们分开。

abstract.en: Naming the substance rather than the drink is a way of making a social habit sound clinical.
abstract.cn: 用物质而非饮品来命名，是一种让社交习惯听起来像临床问题的方式。

examples.en: The doctor asked how much alcohol he drank each week.
examples.cn: 医生问他每周喝多少酒。

examples.en: This cleaner contains alcohol and should not be used near a flame.
examples.cn: 这种清洁剂含酒精，不应在明火附近使用。

examples.en: Sugar alcohols are used as sweeteners in many processed foods.
examples.cn: 糖醇被用作许多加工食品的甜味剂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱抠喝」——爱抠着瓶子喝的人，桌上少不了酒精。

root: 源自阿拉伯语 al-kuḥl「锑粉、精细提炼之物」，经中世纪拉丁语进入英语，先指粉末，后指蒸馏酒，最终固定为乙醇。

sensesIntro.en: One substance runs through all three senses: the chemical itself, the drinks built on it, and the whole family of related compounds.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项贯穿着同一种物质：化学物质本身、以它为基础的饮品，以及整个相关的化合物家族。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass bottle of clear liquid with nothing on the label but a chemical formula.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着透明液体的玻璃瓶，标签上只有一行化学式。

branches.en: a swab of clear liquid on a laboratory bench
branches.cn: 实验台上的一小摊透明液体

branches.en: glasses filled at a dinner table
branches.cn: 餐桌上被斟满的杯子

branches.en: a bottle kept on the top shelf
branches.cn: 放在最上层架子上的那瓶酒

branches.en: a formula written on a whiteboard
branches.cn: 白板上写下的一条化学式

branches.en: one liquid, named by its chemistry and by its effects
branches.cn: 同一种液体，既按化学命名，也按效果命名

intro.en: An Arabic article and noun, their Latin and English descendants, and the endings that build the family.
intro.cn: 阿拉伯语冠词与名词、它们的拉丁语与英语后裔，以及构成词族的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word entered Latin from Arabic as alcohol; it is not a native Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词从阿拉伯语进入拉丁语作 alcohol，并非拉丁语本族词根。

containing alcohol, or a dependent drinker

definition_zh: 含酒精的；酗酒者；酒精依赖者
definition_en: containing alcohol, or a person who cannot control their drinking
core_image: 一只杯子上贴着成分标签，另一只杯子被推到了一边
scene: 聚会上有人把杯子轻轻推开，另拿了一瓶没有标签的饮料。He ordered an alcoholic drink, then changed his mind.
sceneCN: 这里 alcoholic 是「含酒精的」（第 1 个义项：饮料中含有乙醇）；句意为他点了一杯含酒精的饮料，后来又改了主意。图中可辨识物件：玻璃杯、无标签瓶子、餐巾。

pos.zh: 形容词：含酒精的；与酗酒有关的
名词：酗酒者；酒精依赖者

derivatives.zh: 本词的名词词根，义为「酒精；乙醇」
由本词词根加名词后缀构成，义为「酒精依赖；酗酒成瘾」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不含酒精的」

senses.title: Containing alcohol
senses.definition: of a drink, containing ethanol
senses.definitionCN: 指饮料中含有乙醇
senses.example: He ordered an alcoholic drink, then changed his mind.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯含酒精的饮料，后来又改了主意。
senses.why: The -ic ending turns the substance into an adjective, so alcoholic simply means 'having the quality of alcohol'.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ic 把物质变成形容词，所以 alcoholic 就是「带有酒精性质的」。

senses.title: A person dependent on alcohol
senses.definition: a person who is unable to control their drinking and depends on alcohol
senses.definitionCN: 无法控制饮酒、对酒精产生依赖的人
senses.example: The clinic offers support for alcoholics and their families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为酗酒者及其家人提供支持。
senses.why: Medical writing turned the adjective into a noun for a patient, which is why the word can sound clinical rather than insulting.
senses.whyCN: 医学文献把这个形容词转成指病人的名词，所以这个词听起来偏临床，而不一定是辱骂。

intro.en: Alcoholic is a nineteenth-century medical coinage: the Arabic-derived noun alcohol plus the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: alcoholic 是十九世纪的医学新造词：由阿拉伯语来源的名词 alcohol 加上形容词词尾 -ic。

items.en: The Arabic word named a fine powder and later, through alchemy, a distilled spirit.
items.cn: 这个阿拉伯词原指细粉，后来经炼金术转指蒸馏酒。

items.en: Alchemists used alcohol for any finely purified substance, especially distilled liquid.
items.cn: 炼金术士用 alcohol 指任何精细提纯之物，尤指蒸馏液。

items.en: By the eighteenth century English alcohol meant the intoxicating substance in wine and beer.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，英语 alcohol 已指葡萄酒与啤酒中致醉的物质。

items.en: The adjective alcoholic is coined in medical writing, and the noun for the patient follows soon after.
items.cn: 形容词 alcoholic 在医学文献中被造出，指病人的名词随后出现。

items.en: The adjective widened to any drink containing ethanol, while the noun kept its clinical force.
items.cn: 形容词扩展指任何含乙醇的饮品，名词则保留临床意味。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the alcohol family; the near-meaning group gathers words for strong drink and for people who depend on it.
note.cn: 形近组收 alcohol 词族；近义组收烈酒与依赖酒精者的说法。

entries.definition: The substance itself, ethanol.
The condition of dependence on alcohol.
A related chemical class, named from alcohol minus hydrogen.
entries.definitionCN: 一类相关化合物，名称由 alcohol 减氢缩合而成。

entries.definition: Capable of making someone drunk.
An informal and often critical word for someone who drinks too much.
entries.definitionCN: 对酗酒者带批评意味的口语说法。

entries.definition: Strong distilled drinks considered as a category.

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the noun alcohol and the adjective ending -ic.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：名词 alcohol 与形容词词尾 -ic。

normal.en: Alcohol plus -ic makes the adjective; the same -ic appears in acidic and heroic.
normal.cn: alcohol 加 -ic 构成形容词，acidic、heroic 里的也是同一个 -ic。

normal.en: As a noun it names a patient, so it is better avoided as an insult.
normal.cn: 作名词时它指病人，因此不宜拿来骂人。

normal.en: Non-alcoholic keeps the prefix visible: non- plus alcoholic.
normal.cn: non-alcoholic 里前缀仍然看得见：non- 加 alcoholic。

normal.en: The stress falls on -hol: al-co-HOL-ic.
normal.cn: 重音落在 -hol 上：al-co-HOL-ic。

normal.en: Keep the h: alco-holic, not alco-olic.
normal.cn: 不要丢掉 h：alco-holic，而不是 alco-olic。

abstract.en: One suffix turns a substance into a person, which shows how easily medical language labels an identity.
abstract.cn: 一个词尾把一种物质变成一个人，说明医学语言多容易给人贴上身份标签。

abstract.en: The adjective describes a drink; the noun describes a life, and the gap between them is the whole social weight of the word.
abstract.cn: 形容词描述一杯饮料，名词描述一种人生，两者之间的落差就是这个词的全部分量。

abstract.en: Because the word is clinical, saying it about someone carries a diagnosis rather than an opinion.
abstract.cn: 由于这个词带临床色彩，用它说某个人，等于给出诊断而不是意见。

examples.en: He ordered an alcoholic drink, then changed his mind.
examples.cn: 他点了一杯含酒精的饮料，后来又改了主意。

examples.en: The clinic offers support for alcoholics and their families.
examples.cn: 这家诊所为酗酒者及其家人提供支持。

examples.en: The hotel bar serves both alcoholic and soft drinks.
examples.cn: 酒店酒吧既供应含酒精饮料，也供应软饮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱扣喝立刻」——爱扣着杯子喝，立刻就上了瘾。

root: 由 alcohol「酒精」加形容词词尾 -ic 构成，十九世纪医学用语，后兼指酒精依赖者。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses come from one substance: the adjective describes a drink that contains it, the noun describes a person controlled by it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都出自同一种物质：形容词描述含有它的饮料，名词描述被它控制的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one glass labelled with its contents, another glass quietly pushed aside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只标着成分的杯子，另一只被悄悄推到一边。

branches.en: a bottle with a percentage on the label
branches.cn: 标签上标着度数的瓶子

branches.en: a menu divided into soft and strong
branches.cn: 分成软饮与烈酒两栏的酒单

branches.en: a chair in a support group circle
branches.cn: 互助小组围坐的一把椅子

branches.en: a hospital chart with a diagnosis
branches.cn: 写着诊断的病房记录

branches.en: one substance, described first as a quality and then as a fate
branches.cn: 同一种物质，先被描述为一种性质，再被描述为一种命运

intro.en: The noun alcohol, its Arabic source, and the adjective ending that turns it into a description.
intro.cn: 名词 alcohol、它的阿拉伯语来源，以及把它变成描述性词语的形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word reached Latin from Arabic; the list gives the Arabic elements and the Latin form.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词从阿拉伯语进入拉丁语；列表中给出阿拉伯语成分与拉丁语形式。

definition_zh: 警觉的；机敏的；警报；提醒；使警觉
definition_en: watchful and quick to notice things, a warning of danger, or to warn someone
core_image: 守夜人站在塔顶，耳朵转向黑暗里最轻的一声响
scene: 夜里仓库的灯忽然全亮了，值班的人抓起对讲机。A security alert emptied the building within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 alert 是「警报」（第 2 个义项：提示危险、要求立即行动的警告）；句意为一条安全警报让整栋楼在几分钟内清空。图中可辨识物件：对讲机、应急灯、仓库门。

pos.zh: 形容词：警觉的；机敏的
名词：警报；警戒状态
动词：使警觉；提醒；向……报警

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「警觉地」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「警觉；机敏」
由 hyper- 加本词构成，义为「过度警觉的」

senses.title: Watchful and quick
senses.definition: paying close attention and ready to notice or react to something quickly
senses.definitionCN: 高度注意、能迅速察觉或反应的状态
senses.example: Drivers must stay alert on long night journeys.
senses.exampleCN: 长途夜间行车时司机必须保持警觉。
senses.why: The Italian source is a military lookout phrase, 'on the watch', so the adjective began as a description of a guard on duty.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的意大利语来源是军中的瞭望口令「处在警戒中」，所以形容词最初描述的是值班的哨兵。

senses.title: A warning of danger
senses.definition: a warning or announcement that danger or an emergency is present
senses.definitionCN: 告知危险或紧急情况存在的警告或通告
senses.example: A security alert emptied the building within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 一条安全警报让整栋楼在几分钟内清空。
senses.why: The lookout's shout became the message itself, so the noun names the warning rather than the watchman.
senses.whyCN: 哨兵的喊声变成了讯息本身，于是名词指的是那条警告，而不是守望的人。

senses.title: To warn someone
senses.definition: to warn someone about a danger or to make them aware of something urgent
senses.definitionCN: 就危险警告某人，或使其意识到紧急情况
senses.example: A neighbour alerted us to the smoke in the hallway.
senses.exampleCN: 一位邻居提醒我们走廊里有烟。
senses.why: The verb gives the warning a direction: the lookout's cry is now aimed at a particular person.
senses.whyCN: 动词给警告加上了方向：哨兵的喊声如今是对着某个具体的人发出的。

intro.en: Alert comes from an Italian military phrase meaning 'on the watch', and it still sounds like a sentry's word.
intro.cn: alert 来自一个意为「处在警戒中」的意大利军事短语，至今听起来仍像哨兵的用语。

items.en: All'erta meant 'on the height, on the watch', the position of a lookout on a tower.
items.cn: all'erta 意为「在高处、在警戒中」，指哨兵在塔上的位置。

items.en: French took the phrase as alerte, naming both the watch and the warning cry.
items.cn: 法语借作 alerte，既指警戒，也指警告的喊声。

items.en: English borrowed alerte first as a military order and soon as an adjective meaning watchful.
items.cn: 英语先借作军事口令，很快又用作表示「警觉的」形容词。

items.en: The noun widened to civilian warnings, from fire to weather, and the verb followed.
items.cn: 名词从军事扩展到民用的火警、天气等警告，动词随后出现。

items.en: Modern use ranges from a phone alert to a doctor's alertness, all from the same lookout post.
items.cn: 现代用法从手机警报一直到医生的警觉度，全都出自同一个瞭望岗位。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on alert; the near-meaning group gathers watchfulness and warnings.
note.cn: 形近组收由 alert 构成的词；近义组收警觉与警告类词。

entries.definition: The state of being watchful and quick to react.
In a watchful, attentive manner.
A warning device or the fear it causes.
entries.definitionCN: 警报装置，或它引起的恐惧。

entries.definition: Very careful to notice danger, especially over a long period.
entries.definitionCN: 长期保持警惕、留意危险的。

entries.definition: Attentive and looking out for possible trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 留心、注意可能出现的麻烦的。

entries.definition: A statement or sign that danger may be coming.
entries.definitionCN: 提示危险可能来临的话语或标志。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the Italian phrase all'erta and its French reshaping alerte.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：意大利短语 all'erta 及其法语改写 alerte。

normal.en: Alert and alarm are cousins: one is the watch, the other the cry.
normal.cn: alert 与 alarm 是表亲：一个是守望，一个是呼喊。

normal.en: All'erta means 'on the height', so alert began as a position on a tower.
normal.cn: all'erta 意为「在高处」，所以 alert 最初是塔上的一个位置。

normal.en: Stay alert is an instruction to the eyes and ears, not to the feet.
normal.cn: stay alert 是对眼睛和耳朵下的指令，不是对脚。

normal.en: On alert is the state; an alert is the message; to alert is the action.
normal.cn: on alert 是状态，an alert 是讯息，to alert 是动作。

normal.en: One l, then e: a-l-e-r-t, not allert.
normal.cn: 一个 l 后接 e：a-l-e-r-t，不是 allert。

abstract.en: Alertness is a form of attention that assumes something may go wrong, which is why guards and editors both need it.
abstract.cn: 警觉是一种预设「可能出事」的注意力，所以哨兵与编辑都需要它。

abstract.en: The same word is a state, a message and an action, because a warning only exists across all three.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既是状态、又是讯息、又是动作，因为警告正是在这三者之间才成立。

abstract.en: A society that is permanently on alert eventually stops noticing the alerts.
abstract.cn: 长期处于警戒状态的社会，最终会不再注意那些警报。

examples.en: Drivers must stay alert on long night journeys.
examples.cn: 长途夜间行车时司机必须保持警觉。

examples.en: A security alert emptied the building within minutes.
examples.cn: 一条安全警报让整栋楼在几分钟内清空。

examples.en: A neighbour alerted us to the smoke in the hallway.
examples.cn: 一位邻居提醒我们走廊里有烟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，勒特」——额，勒特一听见动静就竖起耳朵，特别警觉。

root: 源自意大利语军事短语 all'erta「在高处、在警戒中」，经法语 alerte 进入英语，由「瞭望」引申为警觉、警报与报警。

sensesIntro.en: One lookout post produces all three senses: the guard's state, the cry he raises, and the act of raising it for someone else.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都出自同一个瞭望岗位：哨兵的状态、他发出的喊声，以及替别人发出喊声的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watchman on a tower turns his ear towards the faintest sound in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：塔上的守夜人把耳朵转向黑暗中那一声最轻的响动。

branches.en: a driver's eyes moving between mirror and road
branches.cn: 在后视镜与路面之间移动的司机目光

branches.en: a siren and a message on every phone
branches.cn: 响起的警报与每部手机上的通知

branches.en: a neighbour knocking hard on the door
branches.cn: 用力敲门的邻居

branches.en: a red light spinning above an entrance
branches.cn: 门口上方旋转的红灯

branches.en: one watchfulness, kept and passed on
branches.cn: 同一种警觉，自己保持，也传给别人

intro.en: An Italian phrase of place, its French form, and the English endings built on the borrowed word.
intro.cn: 一个表示位置的意大利短语、它的法语形式，以及建在这个借词上的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The phrase is Italian; erta goes back to Latin erectus, 'raised', so the list gives that Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 这个短语属意大利语；erta 可追到拉丁语 erectus「竖起的」，因此列表给出这一拉丁来源。

items.meaning: on the height, on the watch

definition_zh: 外国的；陌生的；格格不入的；外国人；外星人
definition_en: belonging to another country, strange and unfamiliar, or a person from another country or planet
core_image: 一个人站在热闹的街口，四周的话他一句也听不懂
scene: 夜市里人声鼎沸，他站在摊子前，听不懂旁边的人在说什么。The customs officer asked whether he was an alien or a resident.
sceneCN: 这里 alien 是「外国人、外侨」（第 4 个义项：法律意义上不属本国的人）；句意为海关人员问他是外侨还是居民。图中可辨识物件：夜市摊子、行李箱、证件。

pos.zh: 形容词：外国的；陌生的；格格不入的
名词：外国人；外侨；外星人

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「使疏远；使格格不入」
由 alienate 加名词后缀构成，义为「疏离；异化」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「陌生感；异质性」

senses.title: Belonging to another country
senses.definition: belonging to or coming from a country that is not one's own
senses.definitionCN: 属于或来自非本国的国家
senses.example: The plant is an alien species that spread along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物是沿河扩散的外来物种。
senses.why: Latin alienus meant 'belonging to another', so the word marks anything that belongs to someone else's place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alienus 意为「属于他人的」，所以这个词标记的是归属于别人那处地方的东西。

senses.title: Strange and unwelcome
senses.definition: strange, unfamiliar, and therefore difficult to accept or fit into
senses.definitionCN: 陌生、不熟悉，因此难以接受或融入
senses.example: The rules felt alien to everything she had been taught.
senses.exampleCN: 这些规则与她所受的一切教导都格格不入。
senses.why: What belongs elsewhere can also feel wrong here, so the word shifted from ownership to emotional distance.
senses.whyCN: 属于别处的东西，在这里也可能让人觉得不对劲，于是这个词从「归属」转向了情感上的距离。

senses.title: A being from another planet
senses.definition: in science fiction, a creature from another planet
senses.definitionCN: 科幻作品里来自其他星球的生物
senses.example: The film shows an alien learning to speak through music.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片讲一个外星人通过音乐学会说话。
senses.why: Twentieth-century science fiction reused the legal word for a foreigner and moved the border from a country to a planet.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪科幻沿用了这个法律词，把边界从国界搬到了星球之间。

senses.title: A foreign national, in law
senses.definition: in law, a person who is not a citizen of the country in which they are
senses.definitionCN: 法律上不属所在国公民的人
senses.example: The customs officer asked whether he was an alien or a resident.
senses.exampleCN: 海关人员问他是外侨还是居民。
senses.why: Legal writing needed a neutral term for non-citizens, and the old adjective supplied it; the usage is now often replaced by foreign national.
senses.whyCN: 法律文书需要一个中性词指非公民，这个古老形容词正好补位；如今这一用法多被 foreign national 取代。

intro.en: Alien goes back to a Latin word for 'belonging to another', and every sense still turns on that idea of elsewhere.
intro.cn: alien 可追到拉丁语中意为「属于他人」的词，所有义项都围绕「属于别处」这个念头。

items.en: Alius meant 'other', the root of alias, alter and alien alike.
items.cn: alius 意为「其他的」，alias、alter 与 alien 都出自这个词。

items.en: Alienus meant 'belonging to another, foreign', and could describe both persons and things.
items.cn: alienus 意为「属于他人的、外来的」，既可形容人也可形容物。

items.en: French carried the word into law and diplomacy, where it named a person outside the community.
items.cn: 法语把这个词带入法律与外交，用来指群体之外的人。

items.en: English uses alien from the fourteenth century for foreigners and for things that do not belong.
items.cn: 英语自十四世纪起用 alien 指外国人，也指不属于本地的事物。

items.en: Science fiction added the planetary sense in the twentieth century, and the legal sense has since softened.
items.cn: 科幻在二十世纪加入「外星」义，法律义此后逐渐软化。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same 'other' root; the near-meaning group gathers outsiders and unfamiliar things.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「其他」词根的词；近义组收外来者与陌生事物。

entries.definition: To make someone feel unwelcome or distant.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人感到不受欢迎或疏远。

entries.definition: The feeling of being cut off from a group or from oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 与群体或与自我割裂的感觉。

entries.definition: A false name used by a person.
Belonging to a country other than one's own.
A person one does not know.
Unfamiliar in a way that is interesting rather than threatening.
entries.definitionCN: 陌生但有趣，而非令人不安的。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: Latin alius, 'other', and the adjective ending -enus.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：拉丁语 alius「其他的」与形容词词尾 -enus。

normal.en: Alien, alias and alter all begin with the same idea: the other one.
normal.cn: alien、alias、alter 都从同一个念头开始：另一个。

normal.en: Alien to means foreign to, and it is the phrase that carries the emotional sense.
normal.cn: alien to 意为「与……格格不入」，情绪义就藏在这个搭配里。

normal.en: The legal noun is neutral, the science-fiction noun is exciting: context does the work.
normal.cn: 法律名词是中性的，科幻名词是刺激的：意义由语境完成。

normal.en: The stress is on the first syllable: A-li-en.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：A-li-en。

normal.en: Keep the i before the e: a-l-i-e-n.
normal.cn: 注意 i 在 e 前：a-l-i-e-n。

abstract.en: A word for 'belonging to another' can describe a plant, a law, a feeling and a planet, because otherness takes many forms.
abstract.cn: 一个「属于他人」的词既能形容植物、法律、感受，也能形容星球，因为「他者」有许多形态。

abstract.en: The same word that excludes can also fascinate, which is why alien and exotic sit so close together.
abstract.cn: 同一个用于排斥的词也能令人着迷，所以 alien 与 exotic 靠得那么近。

abstract.en: Calling someone an alien is always a statement about the border, not about the person.
abstract.cn: 把某人称作 alien，说的永远是边界，而不是那个人。

examples.en: The customs officer asked whether he was an alien or a resident.
examples.cn: 海关人员问他是外侨还是居民。

examples.en: The rules felt alien to everything she had been taught.
examples.cn: 这些规则与她所受的一切教导都格格不入。

examples.en: The film shows an alien learning to speak through music.
examples.cn: 这部影片讲一个外星人通过音乐学会说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱连」——爱连家乡都不认识他，他成了这里的外人。

root: 源自拉丁语 alienus「属于他人的、外来的」，其词根 alius 意为「其他的」。

sensesIntro.en: One idea of elsewhere runs through all four senses: another country, another culture, another planet, and the legal line drawn around a community.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项贯穿着同一个「别处」：别的国家、别的文化、别的星球，以及围绕共同体划下的那条法律界线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller stands at a busy corner and understands not one word around him.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个旅人站在热闹的街口，周围的话一句也听不懂。

branches.en: a plant that spreads where it was never native
branches.cn: 在并非原生之地蔓延的植物

branches.en: a rule book written in a language of its own
branches.cn: 用另一套语言写成的规则手册

branches.en: a light crossing the sky too fast to be a plane
branches.cn: 快得不像飞机的天上光点

branches.en: a form with two boxes: citizen and other
branches.cn: 只有「公民」与「其他」两栏的表格

branches.en: one outside position, felt and also filed
branches.cn: 同一个「在外」的位置，既被感受，也被归档

intro.en: A Latin root for 'other', its adjective, and the English endings that build the family.
intro.cn: 一个意为「其他」的拉丁词根、它的形容词形式，以及构成词族的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: alius and alienus are recorded Latin; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: alius 与 alienus 都是有文献记录的拉丁词，更早的印欧词根属重构。

items.meaning: the state of being cut off

definition_zh: 使排成直线；对齐；使一致；校准
definition_en: to place things in a straight line, to make ideas or policies agree, or to adjust a device precisely
core_image: 三枚钉子被打在同一根拉紧的线上，一个也不偏
scene: 工人蹲在地上，眯起一只眼睛，把两块木板推到同一条线上。He aligned the shelf with the edge of the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 align 是「使对齐、排成直线」（第 1 个义项：把物体摆到同一条线上）；句意为他让架子与墙边对齐。图中可辨识物件：木板、拉线、水平尺。

pos.zh: 动词：使排成直线；对齐；使一致；校准

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「排列；一致；联盟」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「使错位、未对齐」
由 misalign 加名词后缀构成，义为「错位；不对齐」

senses.title: To put in a straight line
senses.definition: to place two or more things so that they form a straight line or match up exactly
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多物体摆成一条直线，或使其位置完全对应
senses.example: He aligned the shelf with the edge of the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他让架子与墙边对齐。
senses.why: The French phrase à ligne means 'into line', and the verb still performs exactly that physical act.
senses.whyCN: 法语短语 à ligne 意为「成一条线」，而这个动词至今做的正是这个物理动作。

senses.title: To bring into agreement
senses.definition: to make plans, policies, or interests agree with one another
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、政策或利益彼此吻合
senses.example: The two departments aligned their budgets before the review.
senses.exampleCN: 两个部门在评审前把预算口径统一了。
senses.why: Once things are on one line, they point the same way, so the physical image became a political and managerial one.
senses.whyCN: 物体一旦落在一条线上，就指向同一个方向，于是这个物理画面变成了政治与管理上的说法。

senses.title: To adjust a device precisely
senses.definition: to adjust parts of a machine or instrument so that they work in the correct relative position
senses.definitionCN: 调整机器或仪器的部件，使其处于正确的相对位置
senses.example: The mechanic aligned the front wheels after the repair.
senses.exampleCN: 修好之后，技师做了前轮定位。
senses.why: Machines need their parts on the same axis, so the general idea of lining up became a technical procedure with a name.
senses.whyCN: 机器需要各部件处在同一轴线上，于是「排成线」这个一般观念变成了一道有名字的技术工序。

intro.en: Align is a French phrase pulled into English as a verb: à ligne, 'into line'.
intro.cn: align 是一个被英语吸收为动词的法语短语：à ligne，意为「成一条线」。

items.en: Linea meant 'a line, a string', and it is the source of line and of align.
items.cn: linea 意为「线、绳」，是 line 与 align 的共同来源。

items.en: The phrase à ligne, 'into line', described soldiers or objects set in a row.
items.cn: 短语 à ligne「成一条线」用于描述排成一列的士兵或物件。

items.en: French made the verb aligner from the phrase, meaning 'to put into line'.
items.cn: 法语由这个短语造出动词 aligner，意为「摆成一条线」。

items.en: English borrowed aligner as align, first in military and surveying contexts.
items.cn: 英语借入作 align，最初用于军事与测量场合。

items.en: The figurative sense of aligning policies or interests is a twentieth-century extension.
items.cn: 「使政策或利益一致」的比喻义是二十世纪的扩展。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on align; the near-meaning group gathers ways of matching things up.
note.cn: 形近组收由 align 构成的词；近义组收使事物彼此对应的说法。

entries.definition: The state of being in line, or an alliance of interests.
entries.definitionCN: 成一条线的状态，或利益上的结盟。

entries.definition: To put out of line or out of agreement.
A state of being wrongly positioned.
To arrange people or things in a row.
To make different activities work together smoothly.
To change something slightly so that it works or fits better.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微改变某物使其更合适或更好用。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the Latin noun linea and the French phrase à ligne.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：拉丁名词 linea 与法语短语 à ligne。

normal.en: Align is 'a line' turned into a verb: to put things a-line.
normal.cn: align 就是把「一条线」变成动词：把东西摆成一条线。

normal.en: The same word works on shelves, budgets and wheels, because all three need to sit on one axis.
normal.cn: 同一个词能用于架子、预算与车轮，因为三者都需要落在同一轴线上。

normal.en: Alignment is the noun; misalignment adds the idea of going wrong.
normal.cn: alignment 是名词；misalignment 加上了「出了偏差」的意思。

normal.en: Non-aligned countries stay outside a bloc, literally off the line.
normal.cn: non-aligned 国家置身集团之外，字面上就是「不在那条线上」。

normal.en: One l, then i: a-l-i-g-n, and the g is silent.
normal.cn: 一个 l 后接 i：a-l-i-g-n，其中 g 不发音。

abstract.en: Alignment is a physical idea that becomes a moral one: people who agree are said to be on the same line.
abstract.cn: 对齐本是物理观念，后来成了道德观念：意见相同的人被说成在同一条线上。

abstract.en: To align interests is to admit that they were not aligned before.
abstract.cn: 说「使利益一致」，就等于承认此前并不一致。

abstract.en: A machine out of alignment still runs, which is why small misalignments are the hardest to notice.
abstract.cn: 失准的机器照样能转，所以轻微的错位最难被察觉。

examples.en: He aligned the shelf with the edge of the wall.
examples.cn: 他让架子与墙边对齐。

examples.en: The two departments aligned their budgets before the review.
examples.cn: 两个部门在评审前把预算口径统一了。

examples.en: The mechanic aligned the front wheels after the repair.
examples.cn: 修好之后，技师做了前轮定位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，来嗯」——额，来，嗯，把桌角都摆到一条线上。

root: 源自法语短语 à ligne「成一条线」及其动词 aligner，词根为拉丁语 linea「线」。

sensesIntro.en: One line runs through all three senses: objects on it, plans on it, and machine parts on it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项贯穿着同一条线：物体落在线上、计划落在线上、机器部件也落在线上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three nails driven along a taut string, none of them off by a hair.
core.cn: 核心意象：三枚钉子沿一根拉紧的线钉下，一枚也不偏。

branches.en: a shelf pushed level with a wall edge
branches.cn: 被推到与墙边齐平的架子

branches.en: two budgets rewritten to the same assumptions
branches.cn: 按同一套假设重写的两份预算

branches.en: front wheels set on a measuring rig
branches.cn: 在测量架上校准的前轮

branches.en: a party agreeing to a coalition platform
branches.cn: 同意同一份联合纲领的政党

branches.en: one straight line, drawn by hand and by instrument

intro.en: A Latin noun for a line, the French phrase built on it, and the English endings that extend it.

definition_zh: 相像的；相似的；同样地；一视同仁地
definition_en: similar in appearance or character, or in the same manner
core_image: 两只并排摆着的白瓷杯，形状、花纹与缺口几乎一模一样
scene: 双胞胎姐妹穿着一模一样的校服走进礼堂，连班主任都愣了一下。The twins looked so alike that even their teachers confused them.
sceneCN: 这里的 alike 是「相像的」（第 1 个义项：外观或性质相似）；句意是这对双胞胎长得太像，连老师都会认错。

pos.zh: 形容词：相像的；相似的（多作表语）
副词：同样地；一视同仁地

derivatives.zh: 同源词，义为「像；如同」，也可作动词「喜欢」
由 like 加名词后缀构成，义为「相似；肖像」
由 like 加 -wise 构成，义为「同样地；此外」
由 un- 加 like 构成，义为「不像；与……不同」
由 alike 加 -ness 构成，义为「相似之处」，使用频率较低

senses.title: Similar to each other
senses.definition: similar to one another in appearance, character, or amount, used mainly after a linking verb
senses.definitionCN: 在外观、性格或数量上彼此相似，主要用在系动词之后作表语
senses.example: The two brothers look very much alike.
senses.exampleCN: 这两兄弟长得非常像。
senses.why: Old English gelic was built from lic, the word for 'body or form'; alike therefore says that two things share one form, and the sense survives in the predicative pattern look alike.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gelic 由 lic「身体、形体」构成，alike 本义就是「共有一个形体」；这一层意思保留在 look alike 这类表语用法里，所以它几乎不作定语放在名词前。

senses.title: In the same way
senses.definition: in the same manner, or equally, with no difference in treatment
senses.definitionCN: 以相同的方式，或平等地、不加区别地对待
senses.example: The law applies alike to citizens and to visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 法律对本国公民和外来访客同样适用。
senses.why: The adverb is the adjective turned into a manner word: if two parties are alike in standing, they are treated alike, and the -ly form never developed because the old form already ended in a suffix.
senses.whyCN: 副词义是把形容词转成方式状语：如果两方地位相像，就会被同样对待。英语里没有再造出 alikely，因为 alike 本身已经带后缀，直接兼作副词。

intro.en: Alike is a Germanic compound whose second half once meant 'body', so the word began as a statement about shared form.
intro.cn: alike 是日耳曼语复合词，后半部分原义为「身体、形体」，因此这个词最初说的是「共有一个形体」。

items.en: *galaikaz is reconstructed as 'having the same form', built from the prefix *ga- and *laikaz 'body, form'.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *galaikaz 一般重构为「具有相同形体」，由前缀 *ga- 与 *laikaz「身体、形体」构成。

items.en: Old English gelic and the variant onlic carried the sense 'like, similar' and were already used after verbs such as beon.
items.cn: 古英语 gelic 及其变体 onlic 表示「相像的」，当时就常放在 beon 这类动词之后使用。

items.en: In Middle English the form ilike appears; the initial vowel was later remade as a-, giving alike by the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 ilike 这一形式，词首元音后来改作 a-，到十六世纪定型为 alike。

items.en: The word settled into predicative use: two things are alike, but one does not normally speak of an alike pair.
items.cn: 这个词固定用于表语位置：可以说两样东西 are alike，但一般不说 an alike pair。

items.en: The phrase young and old alike generalises the adverb sense into 'everyone, without distinction'.
items.cn: young and old alike 这一说法把副词义扩展为「所有人，不加区别」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Germanic root for 'form'; the near-meaning group gathers words of similarity and sameness with different grammar.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「形体」的日耳曼词根；近义组收表示相似与相同的词，语法用法各不相同。

normal.en: Remember a-like: two things sharing one form.

normal.en: It almost never comes before a noun.

normal.en: Look alike and sound alike are the commonest patterns.

normal.en: As an adverb it means 'equally', as in treat them alike.

normal.en: Do not add -ly; alikely does not exist.
normal.cn: 不要加 -ly，英语里没有 alikely 这个词。

abstract.en: Picture two cups turned on a wheel by the same hand.
abstract.cn: 想象同一双手在陶轮上做出的两只杯子。

abstract.en: See two shadows on a wall that move as one.

examples.en: The twin sisters are so alike that people often mistake one for the other.
examples.cn: 这对双胞胎姐妹太像了，人们常把她们认错。

examples.en: Good teachers treat all students alike, whatever their background.

examples.en: Their views on the matter are alike, though they argue about almost everything else.
examples.cn: 他们在这件事上看法相似，尽管几乎其他每件事都要争论。

root: 古英语 gelic 由 lic「身体、形体」加前缀 ge- 构成，本义「同一形体」；中古英语作 ilike，十六世纪词首改作 a-，定型为 alike，并固定用于表语和副词位置。

sensesIntro.en: One idea of shared form yields two uses: describing two things as similar, and treating them in the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「共有形体」的意象生出两种用法：说两样东西相像，以及用同样的方式对待。

branches.en: one sameness, seen in things and in treatment

definition_zh: 活着的；有生气的；仍然存在的；意识到的
definition_en: living and not dead, full of energy, still in existence, or aware of something
core_image: 清晨推开院门，霜下那棵老树又冒出一截嫩绿的新芽
scene: 地震三天后，救援队从塌落的楼板下抬出一名仍在呼吸的工人。Rescuers found the worker still alive under the rubble.
sceneCN: 这里的 alive 是「活着的」（第 1 个义项：未死亡、仍有生命）；句意是救援人员发现那名工人还活在瓦砾下面。

pos.zh: 形容词：活着的；有活力的；仍存在的；察觉到的

derivatives.zh: 同源词，义为「生命；生活」
同源词，义为「居住；活着」
由 life 加 -ly 构成，义为「活泼的；生动的」
由 live 加 -ing 构成，义为「活着的；现存的」
由 life 加 -less 构成，义为「无生命的；死气沉沉的」

senses.title: Living, not dead
senses.definition: having life; not dead, especially after a danger or an accident
senses.definitionCN: 有生命的、未死亡的，尤指经历危险或事故之后仍然活着
senses.example: The fish was still alive when the boy put it back in the river.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩把鱼放回河里时，它还活着。
senses.why: The word is literally 'in life': Old English on life meant 'in a state of being alive', and that locative phrase hardened into one adjective describing a body that still has life in it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「在生命之中」：古英语 on life 意为「处于活着的状态」，这个表示位置的短语凝固成一个形容词，专指仍然带着生命的身体。

senses.title: Full of energy and activity
senses.definition: full of energy, movement, or excitement, often describing a place or a person
senses.definitionCN: 充满活力、动静或兴奋感，常用来形容地方或人
senses.example: The market came alive at dawn, with shouts from every stall.
senses.exampleCN: 天一亮市场就热闹起来，每个摊位都在吆喝。
senses.why: A place that is alive with noise behaves like a living body: it moves, sounds, and cannot be ignored, so the biological word shades into 'bustling'.
senses.whyCN: 一个 alive with noise 的地方就像活着的身体：会动、会响、无法忽视，于是这个生物学词汇引申出「热闹、有生气」的意思。

senses.title: Still in existence
senses.definition: continuing to exist or be used, rather than dying out or being forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 继续存在或被使用，而非消亡、被遗忘
senses.example: The old songs are kept alive by a handful of village singers.
senses.exampleCN: 这些老歌靠村里少数几位歌手传唱而保存下来。
senses.why: If a custom is treated as a living thing, then keeping it alive means feeding it so that it does not die; the metaphor extends life from bodies to practices.
senses.whyCN: 如果把习俗看成一个活物，那么 keep it alive 就是给它养分、不让它死掉；这个比喻把「生命」从身体扩展到风俗、语言和传统。

senses.title: Aware of something
senses.definition: conscious of a fact or danger and therefore responsive to it, used in the phrase alive to
senses.definitionCN: 意识到某个事实或危险因而会作出反应，用于短语 alive to
senses.example: A good editor stays alive to the small shifts in public taste.
senses.exampleCN: 好编辑对公众趣味细微的变化始终保持敏感。
senses.why: To be alive to a risk is to have one's senses switched on towards it, as a living creature is alert to movement in the grass.
senses.whyCN: be alive to a risk 指的是感官朝那个风险打开，就像活物对草丛里的动静保持警觉一样；这里强调的是感知的敏锐，而不是生命本身。

intro.en: Alive began as a phrase meaning 'in life' and only later shrank into a single adjective.
intro.cn: alive 最初是一个意为「在生命之中」的短语，后来才缩合成一个形容词。

items.en: *libam is reconstructed with the sense 'life, body, something left over', and it underlies both life and live.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *libam 一般重构为「生命、身体、留存之物」，它是 life 与 live 的共同来源。

items.en: Old English lif meant 'life, existence, way of living', and the prepositional phrase on life meant 'in life'.
items.cn: 古英语 lif 意为「生命、存在、生活方式」，介词短语 on life 意为「在生命之中」。

items.en: The phrase on life was used predicatively with verbs such as beon: a person was described as being in life rather than as having life.
items.cn: on life 常与 beon 这类动词连用作表语：说的是一个人「处在生命之中」，而不是「拥有生命」。

items.en: The phrase fused into one word, spelled alife, alyve, or alive, and the initial a- was no longer felt as a preposition.
items.cn: 这个短语融合成一个词，拼作 alife、alyve 或 alive，词首的 a- 已不再被感知为介词。

items.en: Modern English keeps alive in predicative position and extends it to places, traditions, and awareness, while the attributive slot belongs to living.
items.cn: 现代英语让 alive 固定作表语，并把它扩展到地方、传统与感知；定语位置则由 living 承担。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the old root for life; the near-meaning group holds words for being alive or aware, each with its own grammar.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「生命」的古老词根；近义组收表示「活着」或「察觉」的词，语法位置各不相同。

abstract.en: Picture a green shoot pushing through frozen soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一截嫩芽顶开冻土。

examples.en: The doctors worked all night to keep the injured driver alive.
examples.cn: 医生们整夜抢救，让受伤的司机活了下来。

examples.en: By midnight the square was alive with music and dancing.

examples.en: She is alive to the danger of trusting strangers online.

sensesIntro.en: From a body that still breathes, alive spreads to busy places, surviving customs, and a mind that notices danger.

definition_zh: 全部的；所有的；一切；完全地；唯一的事物
definition_en: the whole of something, every member of a group, everything, or completely
core_image: 整张摊开的地图，边缘一处也没有被裁掉
scene: 讲座开始前半小时，门口已经排起长队。All the seats were taken before the talk began.
sceneCN: 这里的 all 是「全部的」（第 1 个义项：指整体或每一个成员）；句意是讲座开始前所有座位都被占满了。

pos.zh: 限定词：全部的；所有的
代词：全部；一切
副词：完全地；都

derivatives.zh: 由 all 与 most 合成，义为「几乎；差不多」
由 all 与 way 合成，义为「总是；一直」
由 all 与 one 合成，义为「独自的；单独的」
由 all 与 so 合成，义为「也；而且」
由 all 与 mighty 合成，义为「全能的」

senses.title: The whole of; every member
senses.definition: the whole amount of something, or every member of a group, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的全部数量，或一个群体中的每一个成员，用在名词之前
senses.example: All the windows were closed before the storm arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前，所有窗户都关上了。
senses.why: Old English eall already meant 'the whole, every part', and the determiner use keeps that totalising force directly in front of the noun it covers.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 eall 本义就是「整体、每一部分」，限定词用法把这股「全部包住」的力量直接放在名词前面，所以后面接单数整体或复数成员都可以。

senses.title: Everything
senses.definition: everything, or all things of a kind, used as a pronoun without a following noun
senses.definitionCN: 一切，或某一类的全部事物，作代词使用时不接名词
senses.example: All was quiet in the house after the guests had gone.
senses.exampleCN: 客人走后，屋子里一片寂静。
senses.why: When the noun is left out, the same totality stands on its own as a pronoun; English then treats it as singular, which is why the verb is was, not were.
senses.whyCN: 名词被省略后，同一个「整体」独立成代词；英语把它当单数处理，所以动词用 was 而不是 were，这也是它与 all of them 的区别。

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: entirely or completely, used to strengthen an adjective, a preposition, or a verb
senses.definitionCN: 完全地、彻底地，用来加强形容词、介词或动词
senses.example: The children were all wet after playing in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在雨里玩过之后全身都湿透了。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the idea of totality but applies it to a state rather than a set: if every part of you is wet, you are all wet.
senses.whyCN: 副词保留了「整体」的意思，只是把它从「一组成员」转到「一种状态」上：如果一个人身上每一处都湿了，就是 all wet。

senses.title: The only thing that
senses.definition: the single thing or amount involved, used in clauses such as all I want, where a relative that is usually dropped
senses.definitionCN: 所涉及的唯一事物或数量，用于 all I want 这类从句，其中的关系词 that 通常省略
senses.example: All I need is a quiet room and an hour of sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 我只需要一间安静的房间和一小时睡眠。
senses.why: In this pattern the totality is narrowed to one item by the following clause: the whole of what is wanted consists of that single thing.
senses.whyCN: 在这个句型里，后面的从句把「整体」收窄成一项：想要的全部内容就只是那一件事，所以 all 在这里等于 the only thing。

intro.en: All is one of the oldest totalising words in English, and it has fed a large family of compounds.
intro.cn: all 是英语里最古老的「全部」类词之一，并衍生出一大批复合词。

items.en: *allaz is reconstructed as 'all, whole', with relatives in German all and Dutch al.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *allaz 一般重构为「全部、整体」，德语 all 与荷兰语 al 都是它的亲属。

items.en: eall could modify a noun, stand alone as a pronoun, and combine with adjectives, already covering the three main uses.
items.cn: 古英语 eall 既能修饰名词，也能独立作代词，还能与形容词组合，三种主要用法当时已经具备。

items.en: Middle English reduced the form to al before consonants and all elsewhere, and the doubled l became the modern spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语在辅音前缩作 al，其他位置作 all，双写 l 后来成为现代拼写。

items.en: Compounds such as almost, always, alone, and also were formed from all plus a second element, and their meanings drifted away from the sum of the parts.
items.cn: almost、always、alone、also 这类复合词由 all 加第二个成分构成，词义后来偏离了两部分字面相加的意思。

items.en: Modern English keeps all as determiner, pronoun, and adverb, and fixes several idiomatic phrases such as after all and at all.

definition_zh: 联盟；同盟；结盟关系；（旧）姻亲关系
definition_en: a union of countries or groups formed for a shared purpose, or the relationship created by such a union
core_image: 两户人家把各自的门闩用一根粗绳系在一起
scene: 两个小国面对同一个强敌，签下条约把军队交给同一名指挥官。The two countries formed an alliance against the invaders.
sceneCN: 这里的 alliance 是「联盟」（第 1 个义项：国家为共同目的结成的同盟）；句意是两国结成联盟抵御入侵者。

pos.zh: 名词：联盟；同盟；结盟关系；姻亲关系

derivatives.zh: 同源词，义为「盟友」，也可作动词「结盟」

senses.title: A union of states for a common aim
senses.definition: a formal union of two or more states or governments that agree to act together, especially in war or defence
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个国家或政府为共同行动、尤其在战争或防务上合作而结成的正式联合
senses.example: The two kingdoms sealed an alliance that lasted forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 两个王国缔结了一项持续四十年的同盟。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning 'to bind'; an alliance is literally a binding of separate parties, and states bind themselves by treaty so that each must move with the other.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「捆绑」的动词；alliance 字面上就是把彼此分开的各方绑在一起，国家通过条约把自己绑住，因此一方行动时另一方也受到牵制。

senses.title: A coalition of groups or people
senses.titleCN: 团体或个人的联合；同盟
senses.definition: a union of organisations, parties, or individuals who cooperate for a shared purpose without merging into one body
senses.definitionCN: 组织、政党或个人为共同目标合作而形成的联合，但并不合并为一个整体
senses.example: An alliance of small shops negotiated a lower rent together.
senses.exampleCN: 一些小店铺组成联盟，一起谈下了更低的租金。
senses.why: The binding image transfers easily from states to any parties: what matters is the pledge to act together, not the size of the members, so the word covers shopkeepers and parties as well as nations.
senses.whyCN: 「捆绑」的意象很容易从国家转到任何团体：关键在共同行动的承诺，而不在成员大小，所以小店主、政党乃至个人都能用 alliance 来形容这种联合。

senses.title: Kinship by marriage
senses.definition: a relationship created by marriage between families, an older sense still found in historical writing
senses.definitionCN: 家族之间因婚姻而形成的关系，这是较旧的义项，仍见于历史文献
senses.example: The noble houses sought an alliance through the marriage of their eldest children.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个贵族家族想通过长子女的婚姻建立姻亲关系。
senses.why: Marriage also binds two families, so the same word once served for a political treaty and for a wedding; modern usage keeps the political sense and leaves this one to histories and genealogies.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻同样把两个家族绑在一起，所以这个词过去既指政治盟约也指婚事；现代用法保留了政治义，把姻亲义留给历史与族谱类文本。

intro.en: Alliance is a binding word: it goes back to a Latin verb for tying things together.
intro.cn: alliance 是一个「捆绑」的词：源头是拉丁语中表示把东西系在一起的动词。

items.en: ligare meant 'to tie, bind', and it also produced ligature and obligation.
items.cn: ligare 意为「系、捆、绑」，它还生出 ligature 与 obligation 等词。

items.en: The prefixed verb alligare meant 'to bind to something', with ad- adding the idea of direction towards.
items.cn: 加前缀的动词 alligare 意为「绑到某物上」，ad- 补出「朝向」的方向感。

items.en: Old French alier and its noun form developed the political sense of joining parties by agreement.
items.cn: 古法语 alier 及其名词形式发展出「以协议把各方联合起来」的政治义。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the fourteenth century, first for marriage ties and treaties, then for any league of parties.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个名词，最初指婚姻联系与条约，后来泛指任何团体的联合。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from military alliances to alliances of companies, while the marriage sense survives mainly in historical writing.
items.cn: 现代用法从军事同盟延伸到企业联盟，姻亲义则主要留在历史叙述里。

note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「捆绑」词根；近义组收不同紧密程度的同盟与协定。

definition_zh: 分配；拨给；分派（任务）；把（成本）分摊到科目
definition_en: to give out money, time, or resources for a particular purpose, or to assign a duty or cost to someone
core_image: 一张长桌上摆着几只空盘子，厨师按人数把菜一份份分进去
scene: 市政会议开到深夜，争论的焦点是钱该往哪里花。The council allocated half the budget to road repairs.
sceneCN: 这里的 allocate 是「分配、拨给」（第 1 个义项：把钱或资源按用途分出）；句意是市议会把一半预算拨给了道路维修。

pos.zh: 动词：分配；拨给；分派；分摊

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -tion 构成，义为「分配；拨款；配额」

由动词加 -or 构成，义为「分配者；分配程序」

senses.title: To give out money or resources
senses.definition: to set apart and give out money, materials, or other resources for a stated purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途划出并发放资金、物资或其他资源
senses.example: The hospital allocated two million pounds to new equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 医院拨出两百万英镑购置新设备。
senses.why: Latin locare meant 'to place', and ad- added 'to'; to allocate is to place something into a particular slot, so money is put where the purpose requires it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locare 意为「放置」，ad- 表示「到」；allocate 就是「放到某个位置上」，钱被放进为它指定的那一格，所以既可译「分配」也可译「拨给」。

senses.title: To assign a duty or role
senses.definition: to give a particular job, duty, or role to a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 把某项工作、职责或角色交给某个人或某个群体
senses.example: The teacher allocated each group a different part of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把项目的不同部分分派给各个小组。
senses.why: The same 'placing' works for tasks: a duty is put into someone's hands, and the person becomes the slot it occupies.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「放置」也适用于任务：职责被放进某人手里，那个人就成了这项职责所在的位置，因此 allocate 常与 tasks、duties、roles 搭配。

senses.title: To apportion costs in accounting
senses.definition: to divide a cost or revenue among accounts, departments, or periods in bookkeeping
senses.definitionCN: 在记账中把成本或收入分摊到各科目、各部门或各期间
senses.example: The firm allocated the overhead costs across its three branches.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把间接费用分摊到三个分部。
senses.why: In accounting the 'placing' becomes a division: one total is cut into shares and each share is placed on the account that caused it, which is why the verb appears with costs and overhead.
senses.whyCN: 在会计里，「放置」变成了「切分」：一笔总额被切成若干份，每一份放进造成它的那个科目，所以这个义项的宾语常见 costs、overhead 这类词。

intro.en: Allocate is a bookkeeping word at heart: it comes from a Latin verb for placing something in a spot.
intro.cn: allocate 骨子里是个记账词：它来自拉丁语中表示「把东西放到某处」的动词。

items.en: locus meant 'place, spot', and it also gave English local and locate.
items.cn: locus 意为「地方、位置」，英语的 local 与 locate 也由它而来。

items.en: locare meant 'to place, set, arrange', and was used of putting things or persons in position.
items.cn: locare 意为「放置、安置、安排」，用于把物品或人放到位置上。

items.en: The prefixed form allocare is recorded in medieval Latin with the sense 'to place to, assign', especially in accounts.
items.cn: 加前缀的形式 allocare 见于中世纪拉丁语，义为「放置到、分派」，尤用于账目。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century; early examples already concern money and shares.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，早期用例已经与钱款和份额有关。

items.en: Modern usage extends the verb from budgets to tasks, seats, time slots, and computing memory.
items.cn: 现代用法把它从预算扩展到任务、座位、时间段以及计算机内存。

senses.title: To give permission
senses.definition: to let someone do something by giving permission, often from a position of authority
senses.definitionCN: 以许可的方式让人做某事，通常出自有权的一方
senses.example: The guard allowed us to enter through the side gate.

senses.why: Old French alouer carried the sense 'to grant, permit', and that permissive force is the core of the word: a gate is opened rather than forced.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 alouer 带有「准许、给予」的意思，这股放行的力量是这个词的核心：门是被打开的，而不是被撞开的，所以 allow 默认说话者或主语有一定权限。

senses.definitionCN: 使某个动作或结果成为可能，或未加阻止而任其发生
senses.example: The wide windows allow plenty of light into the room.
senses.exampleCN: 宽大的窗子让大量光线照进房间。
senses.why: When permission is built into a design rather than a person, the same verb describes a space or a tool that leaves room for something to happen.
senses.whyCN: 当「允许」不再来自某个人，而是来自设计本身时，同一个动词就用来描述空间或工具「留出了让某事发生的余地」，于是有了窗户 allow light 这类说法。

senses.title: To set aside an amount of money or time
senses.definition: to plan or set apart a certain amount of money or time for a purpose, especially in a budget or schedule
senses.definitionCN: 为某用途计划或预留一定数量的钱或时间，尤见于预算和日程
senses.example: Allow an hour for the journey in case of traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 路上要留出一小时，以防堵车。
senses.why: A budget that permits a sum is one that has room for it, so allow shifts from granting permission to reserving a quantity inside a plan.
senses.whyCN: 一份「允许」某笔开支的预算，就是给这笔钱留了位置，所以 allow 从「准许」转成「在计划里预留出一个量」，宾语常是 time、money、space。

senses.title: To admit as true
senses.definition: to agree that a statement or fact is true, often reluctantly
senses.definitionCN: 承认某个说法或事实为真，常带不情愿的意味
senses.example: She allowed that the plan had some merit.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认这个计划确有可取之处。
senses.why: This sense grew from the older meaning 'to approve, to praise'; to allow a claim is to let it stand as acceptable rather than to prove it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自较早的「赞许、认可」义：allow 一个说法，是让它站得住、算得上，而不是去证明它，因此语气比 admit 更含蓄。

intro.en: Allow is a word of two Latin streams that merged in French.
intro.cn: allow 由两股拉丁语源流在法语中汇合而成。

items.en: allaudare meant 'to praise', built from ad- and laudare 'to praise', the source of laud and laudable.

items.en: The accounting verb allocare, 'to place to, assign', had a similar form and influenced the French word.
items.cn: 表示记账的 allocare「放置到、分派」形式相近，也影响了法语中的这个词。

items.en: Old French alouer combined the senses of praising, approving, and granting, and it is this blend that English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语 alouer 把称赞、认可与准许几种意思并在一起，英语借入的正是这个混合体。

items.en: Middle English alowen is recorded with the senses 'to praise, approve, permit, and assign'.
items.cn: 中古英语 alowen 的义项包括「称赞、认可、准许、分派」。

items.en: The praise sense faded, leaving permission, possibility, reservation, and admission as the four living uses.

definition_en: a regular sum of money given for a purpose, a permitted amount, or a sum allowed against tax
core_image: 母亲每周把一个封好的小信封放在孩子书桌上
scene: 开学前，父亲把一张卡交给女儿，说每月会往里打钱。Her parents give her a small allowance each month.
sceneCN: 这里的 allowance 是「零用钱、定期给的钱」（第 1 个义项：按固定周期给的一笔钱）；句意是她父母每月给她一笔不多的零用钱。

senses.title: Money given regularly
senses.definition: a sum of money given regularly, especially by a parent to a child or by an employer for a stated purpose
senses.definitionCN: 按固定周期给的一笔钱，尤指父母给孩子的零用钱，或雇主为特定用途发放的补贴
senses.example: He saves half of his weekly allowance for books.
senses.exampleCN: 他每周的零用钱有一半存起来买书。
senses.why: The noun is allow plus -ance: the sum exists because someone has allowed it, so the money carries the trace of permission granted in advance.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是 allow 加 -ance：这笔钱之所以存在，是因为有人「准许」了它，所以津贴一词本身带着预先获准的痕迹。

senses.title: A permitted amount or limit
senses.definition: an amount of something that rules or conditions permit, such as weight, time, or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 规定或条件所允许的数量，如重量、时间或件数
senses.example: Each passenger has a baggage allowance of twenty kilograms.
senses.exampleCN: 每位乘客的行李限额是二十公斤。
senses.why: Here the permission is measured: instead of money, the word marks the ceiling that has been set, so allowance becomes a limit you must stay under.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「准许」被量化了：不再是一笔钱，而是被划出的上限，于是 allowance 变成不能越过的量，常见于行李、时间、配额等语境。

senses.title: A sum allowed against tax
senses.definition: an amount of income that is not taxed, or a sum that may be deducted before tax is calculated
senses.definitionCN: 不需纳税的收入额度，或在计税前可扣除的金额
senses.example: The personal allowance rises slightly next year.
senses.exampleCN: 个人免税额明年会略微提高。
senses.why: Tax law uses the same idea of a permitted portion: a slice of income is allowed to pass untaxed, and that slice takes the name allowance.
senses.whyCN: 税法沿用同一个「获准的部分」概念：一部分收入被允许不计税地通过，这一部分就叫 allowance，所以它既是「免税额」也是「可扣除额」。

senses.title: Consideration for circumstances
senses.definition: the act of taking special circumstances into account and judging someone less strictly, used in make allowance for
senses.definitionCN: 把特殊情况考虑在内而从宽判断，用于短语 make allowance for
senses.example: We should make allowance for the fact that she was ill.
senses.exampleCN: 我们应该体谅她当时生病这一情况。
senses.why: If an amount can be allowed inside a rule, a person can also be granted a margin; the phrase make allowance for transfers the budgeting image to judgement.
senses.whyCN: 既然规则之内可以「留出」一定量，人也同样可以被「留出」一点余地；make allowance for 把预算里的那点余量转用到对人的评判上。

intro.cn: allowance 就是 allow 的名词形式，也继承了它双重拉丁词源的血统。

items.en: The verb alouer meant to grant, approve, or assign, and English took it as allow.
items.cn: 动词 alouer 意为准许、认可、分派，英语借入后作 allow。

items.en: The verb's sense of granting a share produced the need for a noun naming the thing granted.
items.cn: 这个动词「准给一份」的意思，催生了一个指称「所准给之物」的名词。

items.en: The noun allowance is recorded from the fourteenth century with the sense of a sum granted or a stated quantity.
items.cn: 名词 allowance 自十四世纪有记录，义为「准给的款项」或「规定的数量」。

items.en: Trade and colonial accounting fixed the money sense, and transport added the measured sense of weight and space allowed.
items.cn: 商业与殖民时期的账务固定了「钱」的义项，运输业则加上按重量与空间计量的「限额」义。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from pocket money to baggage limits and tax thresholds, with make allowance for keeping the older idea of lenient judgement.
items.cn: 现代用法从零用钱延伸到行李限额与免税额，make allowance for 则保留了「从宽判断」的旧义。

definition_en: a state or person that cooperates with another for a shared purpose, or to join with such a partner

scene: 战事吃紧时，邻国开放了港口供补给船停靠。Britain was a close ally of France during the war.
sceneCN: 这里的 ally 是「盟友、同盟国」（第 1 个义项：战时合作的国家）；句意是战时英国是法国的紧密盟友。

senses.title: A state that supports another
senses.definition: a country that has formally agreed to support another country, especially in war
senses.definitionCN: 正式同意支持另一国家、尤其在战争中提供支持的国家
senses.example: The island remained a loyal ally for over a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛国作为忠诚的盟国持续了一个多世纪。
senses.why: The word goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to bind'; an ally is a state bound to another by treaty, so the relationship is a tie rather than a mere friendship.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自拉丁语中意为「捆绑」的动词；ally 是被条约绑在另一国身边的国家，所以它描述的是一种约束关系，而不只是友好。

senses.title: A person who gives support
senses.definition: a person who helps or supports another in a dispute, campaign, or struggle
senses.definitionCN: 在争执、运动或斗争中帮助或支持他人的人
senses.example: She found a powerful ally in the local newspaper editor.
senses.exampleCN: 她争取到了当地报纸主编这个有力的支持者。
senses.why: Once the binding image leaves the battlefield, any person who stands with you becomes an ally, and the word keeps the sense of a commitment made in a contest.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「捆绑」的意象离开战场，任何站到你这一边的人都可以叫 ally；这个词仍保留着「在较量中立下承诺」的味道，所以比 supporter 更有阵营感。

senses.title: To join forces with
senses.definition: to unite or form a connection with another person, group, or state for a common purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目的与另一人、团体或国家联合或建立联系
senses.example: The small parties allied themselves with the reformers.
senses.exampleCN: 这些小党与改革派联合起来。
senses.why: The verb makes the binding an act: the parties themselves do the tying, which is why it typically appears with with or oneself with.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「捆绑」变成动作：是各方自己动手把彼此系起来，所以它常与 with 连用，或用 ally oneself with 这种反身结构。

items.en: The French verb alier meant 'to unite, combine', and its participle alie gave the noun for a person or party so united.
items.cn: 法语动词 alier 意为「联合、结合」，其分词形式 alie 生出指「被联合的一方」的名词。

items.en: English borrowed ally in the fourteenth century, first for a person joined to another by marriage or treaty.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 ally，最初指因婚姻或条约而与另一方结合的人。

items.en: Warfare fixed the state sense, and the capitalised Allies names the coalition that fought in the two world wars.
items.cn: 战争固定了「国家」这一义项；首字母大写的 Allies 特指两次世界大战中的同盟国阵营。

definition_en: very nearly but not completely, or hardly any when used with a negative word

scene: 列车进站时，车厢里只剩下零星几个人。The train was almost empty when it pulled into the station.

senses.title: Very nearly, but not completely
senses.definition: very nearly, so close to a state or amount that the difference is small but still there
senses.definitionCN: 非常接近某种状态或数量，差别很小但确实存在
senses.example: I almost missed the last bus home.
senses.exampleCN: 我差点错过回家的末班车。
senses.why: The word is a fusion of all and most: 'all the most', that is, as much as possible without reaching the whole, which is exactly the idea of stopping just short.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 all 与 most 的融合，字面近于「全都到了极点」；它指的正是「能到的最大限度，但还差最后一点」，所以天然表示差一点而未完成。

senses.title: Hardly any, with a negative word
senses.titleCN: 几乎没有（与否定词连用）
senses.definition: used before no, nothing, or never to mean that the quantity or frequency is extremely small
senses.definitionCN: 用在 no、nothing、never 之前，表示数量或频率极小，相当于「几乎没有」
senses.example: Almost no one turned up for the early meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 几乎没有人来参加那场早会。
senses.why: When almost modifies a negative, the 'close to' runs in the other direction: it approaches zero rather than the whole, so almost no one means a group that is nearly empty.
senses.whyCN: 当 almost 修饰否定词时，「接近」的方向反了过来：它接近的是零而不是整体，所以 almost no one 指的是一个几乎空掉的群体，而不是「差不多所有人」。

intro.en: Almost is a worn-down compound of all and most, and the parts are still visible in the spelling.
intro.cn: almost 是 all 与 most 磨损后的复合词，两部分在拼写上仍然看得见。

items.en: *allaz 'all' and *maistaz 'most' were separate words with their own histories.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *allaz「全部」与 *maistaz「最多」本是各有来历的两个词。

items.en: ealmæst is recorded with the sense 'almost all, nearly', already a single adverb.
items.cn: 古英语 ealmæst 已是一个副词，义为「几乎是全部、将近」。

items.en: The middle consonant dropped out and the form settled as almost, with the modern spelling by the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 中间辅音脱落，形式定型为 almost，现代拼写约在十五世纪确立。

items.en: Almost became the standard intensifier of near-completion, competing with well-nigh in literary use.
items.cn: almost 成为表示「接近完成」的标准副词，在文学语体里与 well-nigh 竞争。

items.en: Modern usage also fixes the pattern almost no, almost never, where the word points towards zero.
items.cn: 现代用法还固定下 almost no、almost never 这类搭配，此时它指向的是零。

note.cn: 形近组共享 all 加 most 的词根；近义组收表示「接近完成」的副词，程度略有差别。
