definition_zh: 独自的；单独地；仅仅；只有
definition_en: without other people, or only, used to say that nothing else is needed or involved
core_image: 长桌尽头只点着一盏灯，一个人坐在那里吃饭
scene: 孩子们都搬去城里以后，老太太仍住在河边那栋老屋里。She lives alone in the old house by the river.
sceneCN: 这里的 alone 是「独自的」（第 1 个义项：没有其他人在身边）；句意是她独自住在河边的老屋里。

pos.zh: 形容词：独自的；单独的
副词：独自地；仅仅；只有

derivatives.zh: 构词来源，义为「一」，alone 本作 all one
由 alone 截去词首而来，义为「孤单的；单独的」
由 lone 加 -ly 构成，义为「孤独的；寂寞的」
由 lonely 加 -ness 构成，义为「孤独；寂寞」
同由 one 构成，义为「只；仅仅」

senses.title: Without other people
senses.definition: with no other person present or involved, sometimes by choice and sometimes not
senses.definitionCN: 没有其他人在场或参与，可能是自愿，也可能是不得已
senses.example: He ate alone in the kitchen while the party went on next door.
senses.exampleCN: 隔壁在开派对，他一个人在厨房吃饭。
senses.why: The word began as all one: a person reduced to a single unit, with no second party in the scene, and that arithmetic of oneness is still the core.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本作 all one，即「全部只是一个」：一个人被缩减成一个单位，场景里没有第二个，这种「只剩一个」的算法就是它的核心。

senses.title: Only; and nothing else
senses.definition: used after a noun or pronoun to mean that this one thing, and nothing else, is involved or sufficient
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词或代词之后，表示只涉及或只需这一样，别的都不算
senses.example: Money alone will not solve the problem.
senses.exampleCN: 光靠钱解决不了这个问题。
senses.why: If all one means a single item and no more, the adverb naturally excludes everything else, which is why alone after a noun works like only but with a stronger sense of isolation.
senses.whyCN: 如果 all one 指「只有这一项、别无其他」，副词自然就排除掉其余一切；所以名词后的 alone 近似 only，但更强调「孤立地看也只有它」。

senses.title: Leave alone: do not interfere
senses.definition: in the phrase leave someone or something alone, to stop touching, disturbing, or interfering with it
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 leave someone or something alone，表示不再触碰、打扰或干预
senses.example: The doctor told him to leave the wound alone for a few days.
senses.exampleCN: 医生叫他这几天别去碰伤口。
senses.why: To leave a thing alone is to keep it in its state of oneness, adding nothing to it; the phrase turns the adjective into an instruction about non-interference.
senses.whyCN: leave a thing alone 就是让它保持「只有一个」的原样，不再往上面添加任何动作；这个短语把形容词变成了一条「不要干预」的指令。

intro.en: Alone is a phrase that became a word: all one.
intro.cn: alone 是由短语凝成的词：all one。

items.en: The elements eall 'all' and an 'one' were separate words, and the collocation eall an meant 'all one, quite by oneself'.
items.cn: eall「全部」与 an「一」本是两个词，组合 eall an 意为「全部只是一个、完全独自」。

items.en: Middle English wrote the phrase as al one or al oon, still felt as two words.
items.cn: 中古英语把这一短语写作 al one 或 al oon，当时仍被当作两个词。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the phrase was written as one word and had acquired the sense 'solitary, without company'.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，这一短语已连写成一个词，并获得「孤独的、无人陪伴的」意思。

items.en: English later cut off the first syllable to make lone, a word that can stand before a noun, which alone cannot.
items.cn: 英语后来截去词首音节造出 lone，这个词可以放在名词前，而 alone 不能。

items.en: The adverb use 'only' and the phrase let alone developed alongside the original sense of solitude.
items.cn: 副词义「仅仅」与短语 let alone 是在原有的「独处」义之外另行发展出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the one-root; the near-meaning group separates being unaccompanied from feeling unhappy about it.
note.cn: 形近组共享「一」这个词根；近义组区分「无人陪伴」与「因此感到难过」。

definition_zh: 沿着；顺着；向前；与……一起
definition_en: from one end of something towards the other, forward, or together with someone or something
core_image: 一条石板路顺着河岸一直伸向远处的桥
scene: 天快黑时，我们顺着河往桥的方向走。We walked along the river until the lights came on.
sceneCN: 这里的 along 是「沿着」（第 1 个义项：从一端顺着走向另一端）；句意是我们沿着河走，直到灯亮起来。

pos.zh: 介词：沿着；顺着
副词：向前；一起

derivatives.zh: 同源词，义为「长的」，along 本义即「顺着全长」
与 long 同源，义为「长度」
由 along 加 side 构成，义为「在……旁边」
由 be- 加古英语 langian 构成，义为「属于」，与 along 同源

senses.title: Following the length of something
senses.definition: moving or lying in a line that follows the length or edge of something
senses.definitionCN: 沿着某物的长度方向或边缘移动、延伸
senses.example: Poplar trees line the road along the canal.
senses.exampleCN: 运河边的路旁种着白杨。
senses.why: Old English andlang joined and- 'opposite, facing' with lang 'long', so the word originally meant 'the whole length of'; the modern sense still traces a line from one end to the other.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 andlang 由 and-「相对、面对」与 lang「长」构成，本义是「整条长度」；现代义仍然保留了「从一端拉到另一端」这条线。

senses.title: Forward; onward
senses.definition: moving forward or continuing on one's way, used as an adverb after verbs of motion
senses.definitionCN: 向前移动或继续赶路，作副词用在表示移动的动词之后
senses.example: The bus moved along slowly through the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 公交车在人群中缓缓向前移动。
senses.why: If you follow a line to its far end, you are by definition going forward; the adverb keeps that sense of progress without naming the road.
senses.whyCN: 既然沿着一条线走到远端，本身就是向前，所以副词义不必再点出道路，只留下「继续往前」的意思。

senses.title: Together with
senses.definition: in the phrase along with, together with another person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 along with，表示与另一人或另一物一起
senses.example: She sent the letter along with a small gift.
senses.exampleCN: 她把信连同一件小礼物一起寄出。
senses.why: Two things travelling the same line side by side are literally along the same path, and that physical companionship became the idiom along with.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西在同一条线上并排前行，字面上就是「走同一条路」，这种同行的具体画面凝固成了 along with 这个习语。

intro.en: Along began as a word about the full length of something, and its modern uses all keep that line.
intro.cn: along 最初指某物的整条长度，现代各义都保留着这条线。

items.en: *langaz 'long' underlies long, length, and the second element of along.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *langaz「长的」是 long、length 以及 along 后半部分的来源。

items.en: andlang combined and- 'facing, opposite' with lang 'long' and meant 'the whole length of, throughout'.
items.cn: andlang 由 and-「面对、相对」与 lang「长」组合，意为「整条长度、从头到尾」。

items.en: The form along appears in Middle English, and the prepositional use with rivers, roads, and walls becomes common.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 along 这一形式，与河流、道路、城墙搭配的介词用法变得常见。

items.en: The adverb 'forward, onward' develops from the idea of continuing the length of a route.
items.cn: 副词义「向前、继续」由「走完一条路线的长度」这一想法发展而来。

items.en: The phrases along with, get along, and all along fix the word in modern idiom.
items.cn: along with、get along、all along 等短语把这个词固定在现代习语中。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the long root; the near-meaning group gathers prepositions and adverbs of following a line or moving forward.
note.cn: 形近组共享「长」这个词根；近义组收表示「顺着一条线」或「向前」的介词与副词。

senses.title: Next to the side of something
senses.definition: positioned at the side of something and extending in the same direction
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物侧面，并沿同一方向延伸
senses.example: A narrow path runs alongside the railway.
senses.exampleCN: 一条小路与铁路并行。
senses.why: The word is a compound of along and side: it places one thing beside another and keeps the line of the first, which is more precise than the general beside.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 along 与 side 合成：它把一物放到另一物的侧面，同时保持与后者同向延伸，因此比泛指的 beside 更强调「并排且同向」。

senses.title: Together with, as a partner
senses.definition: working or existing together with someone or something, often as an equal partner
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某物共同工作或并存，常含平等合作之意
senses.example: She worked alongside experienced nurses for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 她与经验丰富的护士并肩工作了一年。
senses.why: Two people at the same side of a task stand shoulder to shoulder, so the spatial word becomes a statement about cooperation rather than rank.
senses.whyCN: 在同一项任务的同一边，两个人是并肩站着的，因此这个空间词自然转为「平等合作」的意思，而不含上下级之分。

senses.title: Along the side; to the side
senses.definition: used as an adverb for a ship or vehicle coming up to the side of something, or for moving parallel
senses.definitionCN: 作副词，指船只或车辆靠到某物侧面，或平行移动
senses.example: The pilot brought the boat alongside and cut the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 驾驶员把船靠过来，然后熄了火。
senses.why: Nautical use fixed the adverb: a vessel comes alongside when its side meets the side of a dock or another ship, and the image is purely physical.
senses.whyCN: 航海用法固定了这个副词：当船的一侧贴到码头或另一艘船的侧面时，就说 come alongside，画面完全是物理性的「靠边」。

intro.en: Alongside is a transparent compound of along and side, and it grew up around ships.
intro.cn: alongside 是 along 与 side 的透明复合词，成长于航海语境。

items.en: andlang meant 'the whole length of', combining and- 'facing' with lang 'long'.
items.cn: andlang 意为「整条长度」，由 and-「相对」与 lang「长」构成。

items.en: side meant 'flank, the long edge of a body or object', and it is the same word as modern side.
items.cn: side 意为「侧面、身体或物体的长边」，与现代 side 是同一个词。

items.en: The compound alongside is recorded in the seventeenth century, first in descriptions of ships lying next to one another.
items.cn: 复合词 alongside 在十七世纪有记录，最初用于描述船只并排停靠。

items.en: Come alongside became a standard order at sea, and from the harbour the word spread to roads, buildings, and people.
items.cn: come alongside 成为海上的标准说法，这个词又从港口扩展到道路、建筑与人。

items.en: Modern usage adds the figurative sense of working alongside someone as an equal.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了「与某人平等并肩工作」的比喻义。

normalIntro.en: Alongside simply puts a thing along the side of another, then lets that posture mean partnership.
normalIntro.cn: alongside 就是把一物放在另一物侧边、与之同向，再由这个姿势引申出合作。

normal.en: Along plus side: along the side.
normal.cn: along 加 side：沿着侧面。

normal.en: It suggests a shared direction, unlike plain beside.
normal.cn: 它暗示同一方向，与单纯的 beside 不同。

normal.en: Work alongside is the common figurative pattern.
normal.cn: work alongside 是常见的比喻搭配。

normal.en: At sea, come alongside means to draw up to a dock.
normal.cn: 海上 come alongside 意为靠泊。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节。
